# ionhour_job (Resource)

A heartbeat job: your code pings Ionhour and the job goes LATE, then DOWN, when pings stop.

~> `ping_token` and `ping_url` are stored in Terraform state in plain text. Use an encrypted remote backend. Reading them back needs a READ_WRITE key with `mcp:jobs` (or `mcp:signals`) and MEMBER role or higher; otherwise they are null.

Changing `project_id` moves the job in place and keeps its id and ping token. Import by numeric id or `slug:<slug>`.

~> **Importing an auto-provisioned job.** Jobs created by slug-mode SDK pings carry a slug that those pings depend on. Set the same `slug` in configuration before importing: otherwise the next apply clears it and slug-mode pings (`/signals/s/<slug>`) stop resolving.

Legacy jobs created from an unparseable schedule have no interval. They import with `interval_seconds = null`, and the next apply writes `3600` (or the configured value).

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "ionhour_job" "nightly_backup" {
  name             = "Nightly backup"
  slug             = "nightly-backup"
  project_id       = ionhour_project.payments.id
  interval_seconds = 86400
  grace_seconds    = 1800
}

# Hand the ping URL to the system that runs the job, e.g. a secret store.
output "nightly_backup_ping_url" {
  value     = ionhour_job.nightly_backup.ping_url
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Job name (1-255 characters).
- `project_id` (Number) Project the monitor belongs to. Changing it moves the monitor in place (same id).

### Optional

- `down_severity` (String) Incident severity when the monitor goes DOWN (`P1`-`P4`). Defaults to `P1`.
- `grace_seconds` (Number) Lateness tolerated before the job goes LATE, in seconds (5-86400). Defaults to `300`.
- `interval_seconds` (Number) Expected ping interval in seconds (10-604800). Defaults to `3600`.
- `late_severity` (String) Incident severity when the monitor goes LATE (`P1`-`P4`). Defaults to `P3`.
- `mute_notifications` (Boolean) Suppress notifications. Defaults to `false`.
- `slug` (String) Unique per workspace (`^[a-z0-9_-]{1,64}$`). Lets SDKs ping by slug and addresses the job as `slug:<slug>`. Removing it clears the slug; deleting the job releases it.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Creation time (RFC 3339, UTC).
- `id` (Number) Numeric job id.
- `paused` (Boolean) Whether the monitor is paused (status `PAUSED`). Pause and resume are not managed by Terraform.
- `ping_token` (String, Sensitive) Heartbeat credential for `/api/signals/ping/<token>`. Never rotated by updates. Null unless the API key is READ_WRITE, projects to MEMBER or higher and covers `mcp:jobs` or `mcp:signals`. Sensitive: anyone holding it can send OK heartbeats.
- `ping_url` (String, Sensitive) Full heartbeat URL for this job. Null whenever `ping_token` is null. Sensitive.
- `status` (String) Current status: `NEW`, `OK`, `LATE`, `DOWN`, `PAUSED` or `RESUMED`.
- `updated_at` (String) Last update time (RFC 3339, UTC).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import a job by its numeric id ...
terraform import ionhour_job.nightly_backup 456

# ... or by its slug.
terraform import ionhour_job.nightly_backup slug:nightly-backup

# A job auto-provisioned by a slug-mode SDK ping depends on its slug. Put the
# same slug in configuration BEFORE importing it, for example
#   slug = "nightly-backup"
# otherwise the next apply clears the slug and slug-mode pings
# (/signals/s/nightly-backup) stop resolving.
#
# Legacy jobs created from an unparseable schedule have no interval: they
# import with interval_seconds = null, and the next apply writes 3600 (or the
# value in configuration).
```
